subsystems.name: Injectable mesh scaffold
subsystems.role: provides a flexible, biocompatible substrate that can be injected as a compact bundle and unfold to intercalate with neurons.
parts: conductive traces (gold, platinum, or conductive polymers)

subsystems.name: Nanoelectronic components
subsystems.role: record and stimulate neuronal activity at high density.

subsystems.name: Biocompatible coating
subsystems.role: minimises immune rejection and promotes stable integration with tissue.

subsystems.name: Self-assembly mechanism
subsystems.role: allows the injected mesh to deploy and connect without a surgical opening.
parts: chemical or physical cues for unfolding

subsystems.name: External transceiver
subsystems.role: powers the implant and transmits neural data wirelessly through the skull.

subsystems.name: Delivery system
subsystems.role: injects the mesh into the cortex with minimal damage.

buildSteps.title: Design the mesh layout
buildSteps.detail: A 2D pattern of conductive traces and electrodes is designed on a flexible polymer sheet, with openings that allow cells to weave through after deployment.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the nanoelectronics
buildSteps.detail: Standard cleanroom techniques (photolithography, etching, evaporation) pattern gold or platinum electrodes and interconnects onto the polymer, then the mesh is released from its carrier wafer.

buildSteps.title: Add active components and wireless links
buildSteps.detail: Thin-film transistors, multiplexers, and tiny antennas or ultrasound receivers are integrated to reduce the number of external wires.

buildSteps.title: Coat for biocompatibility
buildSteps.detail: The mesh is coated with anti-inflammatory drugs, growth-promoting peptides, or hydrogels to reduce scarring and encourage neurons to grow close to the electrodes.

buildSteps.title: Load into a delivery device
buildSteps.detail: The flexible mesh is rolled or folded into a needle or catheter small enough (hundreds of micrometres) to inject into the cortex.

buildSteps.title: Inject into the brain
buildSteps.detail: The mesh is injected into the target region, where it unfolds and spreads to cover a volume of tissue, intercalating with neurons.

buildSteps.title: Self-assemble and integrate
buildSteps.detail: Over days to weeks, the mesh deploys fully, and surrounding neurons and glial cells grow around and through it, forming stable electrical junctions.

buildSteps.title: Establish wireless communication
buildSteps.detail: An external headpiece or implanted transceiver powers the mesh and streams neural data out through the skull.

buildSteps.title: Chronic operation and maintenance
buildSteps.detail: The system records or stimulates for months to years, with ongoing efforts to manage immune response and signal degradation.

prerequisites.why: polymers like SU-8 and parylene, and noble-metal conductors, are already used in implantable devices and can be microfabricated into injectable meshes.
rigid arrays (e.g. Utah and Michigan probes) exist, but injectable mesh versions that integrate smoothly with tissue are still in animal research.

prerequisites.tech: Wireless power and data transmission in tissue
prerequisites.why: ultrasound and RF links have been demonstrated in small implants, but scaling to thousands of electrodes through the skull remains difficult.

prerequisites.tech: Long-term neural integration and immune tolerance
prerequisites.why: the brain's foreign-body response degrades signals over time; preventing it without drugs or genetic modification is unsolved.
autonomous nanobots that self-assemble into a conductive web are speculative; current work focuses on passive mesh electronics delivered by syringe.

pathway.milestone: injectable mesh electronics demonstrated in rodent brains, recording neural activity for months
pathway.unlocks: proof that flexible, syringe-delivered electronics can integrate with living tissue.

pathway.milestone: larger-animal studies with wireless power and data, and improved longevity
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the approach can scale to human-sized brains.

pathway.milestone: first human trials for medical restoration (e.g. paralysis or epilepsy)
pathway.unlocks: clinical data on safety and long-term stability.

pathway.milestone: high-bandwidth, bi-directional interfaces for cognitive enhancement and direct communication
pathway.unlocks: new forms of human-machine interaction, if ethical and technical hurdles are overcome.
